0.0.n: Comes directly before a noun, pointing to something near the speaker.

0.1.n: Written in katakana here; it refers to the promotional sheet the reader has received.

0.2.n: Marks このチラシ as the thing obtained in the expression 手にする.

0.3.n: Part of 手にする, an expression for getting or obtaining something.

0.4.n: Links 手 to する in 手にする, literally putting something into one's hand.

0.5.n: Past form of する; together with 手に, it describes what あなた has done.

0.6.n: Directly addresses the reader; the preceding phrase identifies them as someone who received this flyer.

1.0.n: Describes 島, using な to connect it to the noun.

1.1.n: Connects 特別 to 島 so it describes the island.

1.2.n: The destination of the invitation, marked by へ.

1.3.n: Marks the destination and is pronounced え when used as a particle.

1.4.n: ご adds politeness to 招待; the noun alone works as a promotional announcement.

0.lit: You who took this flyer into your hand.
0.tip: このチラシを手にした comes before あなた, describing which person is being addressed.

1.lit: To a special island, an invitation!
1.tip: Japanese promotional lines often omit the verb, so ご招待 alone conveys that you are invited.
